candidats.titre: File:Building at 2629-2635 Main Street and 2387-2395 Fillmore Avenue, Buffalo, New York - 20220801.jpg
candidats.description: The building at the southeast corner of Main Street and Fillmore Avenue in Buffalo, New York is seen in this August 2022 photo. Built in 1916, the original design by architect Colson & Hudson of this two-story mixed-use structure, once characterized by an exterior of buff brick with Indiana limestone trim, is now largely hidden by modern Dryvit siding. However, some features can still be discerned, notably the arched window surrounds on the second floor, pilaster strips spaced periodically on the façade, and the cornice and stepped parapet lining the flat roof. candidats.description: This one-story brick commercial building is rectangular in form with a flat roof and parapet. The front façade (east) reveals a post-World II modernist upgrade to appear sleeker and more modern.

Old buildings on John Bright Street in Birmingham. Was several theatre related lorries down here - possibly for Britain's Got Talent? This is Roseberry Buildings on John Bright Street. Roseberry Buildings of 1902-3, was showrooms for the early car maker Heron, with workshop at the rear. A quirky, slightly sinister design with very free flat-topped gables, canted windows, and a corner turret with a sharp prow. From Pevsner Architectural Guides: Birmingham by Andy Foster. candidats.description: Car showroom and workshops, 1938-39, by Howard and Souster. MATERIALS: steel-framed and reinforced concrete structure, walls of brick faced with reconstituted-stone blocks, now painted white. Roof of reinforced concrete and steel frame with metal sheeting. Floors of reinforced concrete with Terrazzo, rubber and grano finishing. Steel casement windows. PLAN: irregular L-shape plan with showroom, offices (now snooker club) and car storage to the west facing onto Mill Street (this block is known as Len House), and workshops and administration block to the east, facing on to Len Pond.
